verdict.root_cause: Two minutes before onset, platform-automation updated shippingservice's image reference to a demo artifact whose tag names a different service (adservice), with no revert recorded unlike the four prior apply/revert cycles [tr_9febbf74c6c7]. The container that came up is not the shipping binary: shipping's logs shift from normal Rust/tonic GetQuote handler pairs earlier in the window to a repeating JVM/OTel bootstrap block every ~60s with zero handler activity from 17:53 to 18:00 — a process that never reaches serving state [tr_0c02ff9adc51]. With nothing listening, checkoutservice's GetQuote client calls fail fast: in every failing trace the deepest error span is checkout's ShippingService/GetQuote client span with no shippingservice server child at ~2ms, while cart, currency, product-catalog and Redis spans are clean [tr_f999417a9398]. Checkout aborts order preparation before payment, matching order-start log lines with no payment/email/message-write completions [tr_a635f5787293], producing the ~19x error-ratio rise that alerted first [tr_9e757c00ecde]. Nothing changed on checkoutservice itself [tr_06ea24e3898c].
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on a wrong artifact running in shippingservice: a change record placing a mis-tagged image 2 minutes before onset with no revert [tr_9febbf74c6c7], shipping's own logs showing a bootstrap-only restart loop in a Java runtime where the healthy service logged in Rust/tonic format [tr_0c02ff9adc51], and caller-side traces where the error terminates on checkout's side of the hop with no shipping server span and sub-3ms duration — the signature of nothing listening, not a slow or erroring handler [tr_f999417a9398]. checkoutservice alerted first but is the noticer: it has no changes at all [tr_06ea24e3898c] and only the shipping hop errors [tr_f999417a9398]. The wider fan-out follows — frontend and loadgenerator are callers above checkout; quoteservice loses inbound traffic from a dead shipping; email, accounting and frauddetection see no order messages because checkout never reaches the message-write stage [tr_a635f5787293]. The mechanism is a running artifact that is not the one that should be running, so restoring the correct image reference is the fix; a bare restart would re-pull the same wrong image.
open_questions: The earliest metric change point is ~17:31:30, ~25 minutes before the image update and coincident with the QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR override being set [tr_9e757c00ecde, tr_9febbf74c6c7]; whether the incident is one continuous failure with two successive causes, or partially recovered after the 17:42 revert, is unsettled.

Errors are bursty with intervals at zero and max ~0.30 [tr_9e757c00ecde], while a fully crash-looping shipping should fail every quote; whether some replicas still ran the correct image is unresolved, and shippingservice emits no calls_total series to confirm server-side onset [tr_f7bdd49397be].

The shipping log selector returns two runtimes under one label and the 15:58-17:53 interval is truncated [tr_0c02ff9adc51], so it is not fully excluded that the JVM restart loop belongs to a co-labelled workload; pod/image inspection would settle it.

alternatives.root_cause: The QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR override pointed shipping's GetQuote at a non-existent quote host, so shipping failed every quote request.
alternatives.why_not: The override was reverted ~13 minutes before onset with no re-application [tr_9febbf74c6c7], and a live shipping process failing an upstream call would still emit a server span under checkout's GetQuote client span, which no failing trace contains [tr_f999417a9398]. It may still explain the earlier 17:31 change point.

alternatives.root_cause: shippingservice is being killed and restarted by the platform (OOM or failing probe) independent of the image change, so it cannot stay up to serve quotes.
alternatives.why_not: The restart loop starts within minutes of a recorded change to a wrong-service image, and the bootstrap output is a different runtime than the healthy service used [tr_9febbf74c6c7, tr_0c02ff9adc51]; no OOM, kill, or limit evidence was found, and the wrong-artifact story explains both timing and runtime mismatch.

proposal.expected_effect: Shipping's logs stop the ~60s JVM/OTel bootstrap block and resume Rust/tonic GetQuote handler pairs; checkoutservice's GetQuote client spans regain a shippingservice server child and stop erroring; checkoutservice error ratio falls from ~0.136 mean toward the ~0.007 baseline. Shipping emits no calls_total series, so confirm from caller-side traces/metrics and logs only.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if checkout error ratio stays elevated while shipping logs look healthy (points instead at the unresolved ~17:31:30 change point / QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR), or if the JVM bootstrap loop continues after rollback (confirming that loop belongs to a co-labelled Java workload, not the shipping binary).
proposal.risk: Prior image reference is recorded as 'None' rather than a concrete tag, so the recreate may land on an unexpected artifact and leave shipping broken. The recreate also destroys the container that pod/image inspection would need to settle the co-label doubt. If some replicas still ran the correct image (bursty errors, min 0, max ~0.30), those are taken down too and errors spike to near-total during the recreate. Does not stop platform-automation from re-applying the bad image next cycle.
proposal.blast_radius: shippingservice during the recreate; checkoutservice sees resets, propagating to frontend and loadgenerator checkout traffic. quoteservice sees GetQuote traffic resume; paymentservice and emailservice see order completions resume.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service fanout originating at checkoutservice and spreading to frontend and its downstream consumers within minutes; nothing here can be dismissed. Fault class is unclear without evidence, though checkoutservice's lead position makes it the natural first dispatch.
